Key Responsibilities Antenatal Care

  • Conduct comprehensive antenatal assessments and risk screenings.
  • Obtain detailed obstetric, medical, surgical, family, and social histories.
  • Monitor maternal and fetal wellbeing throughout pregnancy.
  • Assess fetal growth, fetal heart rate, fetal movements, and maternal health status.
  • Recognize, document, and report high-risk pregnancy indicators.
  • Provide antenatal counseling and health education.
  • Educate women regarding:
    • Nutrition during pregnancy.
    • Birth planning.
    • Pain management options.
    • Breastfeeding preparation.
    • Newborn care.
    • Family planning.
    • Pregnancy warning signs.
  • Support emotional wellbeing and psychosocial needs of expectant mothers.
  • Facilitate referrals to physicians and specialists when required.

Intrapartum Care (Labor & Delivery)

  • Assess women during labor using established clinical guidelines.
  • Monitor maternal vital signs and labor progression.
  • Perform fetal surveillance and fetal heart rate monitoring.
  • Conduct vaginal examinations within scope of practice.
  • Interpret labor findings and identify deviations from normal progress.
  • Provide continuous labor support and advocacy.
  • Promote physiological and woman-centered childbirth practices.
  • Assist mothers with labor positioning, mobility, and comfort measures.
  • Support pharmacological and non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
  • Prepare laboring women for delivery procedures.
  • Conduct normal vaginal deliveries where permitted by regulatory and organizational policies.
  • Assist obstetricians during instrumental or operative deliveries.
  • Anticipate and respond appropriately to obstetric emergencies.
  • Maintain accurate labor and delivery documentation.

Postnatal Care

  • Perform comprehensive maternal assessments following delivery.
  • Monitor recovery during the immediate postpartum period.
  • Assess uterine involution, lochia, pain management, and overall maternal wellbeing.
  • Identify postpartum complications including:
    • Postpartum hemorrhage.
    • Infection.
    • Thromboembolic events.
    • Mental health concerns.
  • Support maternal physical and emotional adjustment following childbirth.
  • Provide discharge education and follow-up instructions.
  • Promote early mobilization and recovery.

Newborn Care

  • Perform immediate newborn assessment and stabilization.
  • Monitor neonatal adaptation during the transition period.
  • Assess newborn vital signs and physical condition.
  • Support skin-to-skin contact between mother and infant.
  • Promote early initiation of breastfeeding.
  • Recognize neonatal complications requiring escalation.
  • Assist with newborn examinations and screening procedures.
  • Administer prescribed medications and immunizations.
  • Educate parents regarding:
    • Newborn feeding.
    • Hygiene and cord care.
    • Safe sleeping practices.
    • Growth and developmental milestones.
    • Immunization schedules.

Breastfeeding Support

  • Encourage and promote exclusive breastfeeding.
  • Assess breastfeeding effectiveness and challenges.
  • Assist mothers with proper positioning and attachment techniques.
  • Support mothers experiencing breastfeeding difficulties.
  • Educate families regarding breast milk expression and storage.
  • Provide evidence-based lactation support and counseling.

Emergency and High-Risk Obstetric Care

  • Identify signs of maternal and fetal deterioration.
  • Initiate emergency interventions within scope of practice.
  • Participate in the management of:
    • Postpartum hemorrhage.
    • Eclampsia and pre-eclampsia.
    • Shoulder dystocia.
    • Cord prolapse.
    • Fetal distress.
    • Neonatal resuscitation.
  • Escalate concerns promptly to physicians and senior clinical staff.
  • Participate in emergency drills and mock code training.

  • Offer emotional support during pregnancy, labor, and postpartum recovery.
  • Respect cultural, religious, and personal preferences.

Licensure

  • Active professional registration as a Midwife.

A plastic surgeon is a surgeon sub-specialist providing attending and consulting surgical services to patients of all ages in Plastic surgery. Provides pre-operative care, including diagnosis, operative care of all major and minor procedures in the field of plastic surgery and post-operative care He maintains efficient and effective care of patients as part of an integrated program of curative and preventive medical services.

Scope

The work is in Johns Hopkins Aramco Healthcare Surgical Department in Dhahran, Al Hasa, Ras Tanura, and Abqaiq.

The Plastic Surgeon work is responsible for attending ambulatory and hospitalized patients of any age group, including cases of all degrees of complexity, which are within their competence and expertise surgeons work at Dhahran Hospital facility to meet established medical ethical and legal rules in the fields of plastic surgery and by observing practices and procedures as required by Johns Hopkins Aramco Healthcare.  Reports to, and be under the supervision of the Chief of Surgical Services Division.  Plastic surgery provides day to day work including management and evaluation of the quality of patient care within their clinical privileges approved by the Credentials and Privileges Committee.  The Chief Surgeon is informed of unusual problems or action taken regarding unusual cases, within their clinical privileges approved by the Credentials and Privileges Committee.

Plastic Surgeon attends ambulatory and hospitalized patients.  Provides surgical expertise in the field of plastic surgery. Work hours are assigned to meet operational needs of the assigned area. Direction is through the Division Chief.

Job Summary

The Specialist Physician shares responsibility with the Consultant Physician for delivering high-quality, evidence-based, and patient-centered care within their division. The role involves diagnosing and treating complex conditions, managing patient care plans, collaborating with a multidisciplinary team, and contributing to the supervision and training of junior medical staff.

Key Responsibilities

  • Patient Care: Conduct comprehensive patient assessments, take medical histories, order and interpret diagnostic tests, and formulate personalized treatment plans for injuries, illnesses, and disorders within the specialty.
  • Treatment and Procedures: Prescribe and administer appropriate medication, therapy, or other specialized medical care and perform necessary procedures/surgeries related to the specialty.
  • Collaboration and Consultation: Liaise and consult with other medical specialists, departments, and support services to ensure holistic and integrated patient care.
  • Documentation: Accurately document all relevant clinical information in a clear and timely fashion in compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.
  • Quality Improvement and Research: Actively participate in quality improvement initiatives, clinical audits, and research activities to enhance patient safety and care standards.
  • Supervision and Education: Provide instruction, guidance, and supervision to junior medical staff, residents, and students.
  • Communication: Communicate clinical information to patients and their families in a timely and compassionate manner, obtaining informed consent for procedures as required.
  • Compliance: Adhere to all hospital departmental and divisional policies, procedures, and DOH regulations, including occupational health and safety guidelines and infection control protocols.

Qualifications and Requirements

  • Education: An MBBS or equivalent degree from a recognized medical school.
  • Post-Graduate Training: Completion of a structured clinical residency or fellowship program in the relevant specialization.
  • Experience: A minimum of 2-3 years of clinical experience post-specialization, depending on the DOH tier classification qualifications and specific hospital requirements.
  • Licensing:
  • DOH License: A valid Department of Health (DOH) Abu Dhabi license or an eligibility letter to practice in Abu Dhabi is highly preferred.
  • Valid Registration: Must provide evidence of a current, valid license from the country of last or current practice.
  • Good Standing: A current Certificate of Good from the relevant licensing authority.
  • Examinations: Successful completion of the DOH licensing exam (may involve an oral assessment depending on the specialty).
  • Skills: Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, problem-solving skills, and a commitment to continuous medical education (CME/CPD).
  • Language: Fluency in English and Arabic is required, and competence in other languages is often a distinct asset.

The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing the daily operations of the Delivery/Labour Room, ensuring the provision of safe, high-quality, evidence-based, and patient-centered care for mothers and newborns.

Responsibilities

  • Lead and supervise the daily operations of the Delivery/Labour Room to ensure the provision of safe, efficient, and high-quality patient care.
  • Provide clinical leadership, guidance, and support to nursing staff, promoting professional development and evidence-based practice.
  • Ensure compliance with hospital policies, infection prevention and control standards, patient safety initiatives, and regulatory requirements.
  • Coordinate and oversee the care of women during labour, delivery, and the immediate postpartum period, ensuring optimal maternal and neonatal outcomes.
  • Monitor staffing levels, prepare duty rosters, and allocate resources to ensure appropriate coverage and efficient workflow.
  • Collaborate with obstetricians, neonatologists, anaesthetists, midwives/nurses, and other multidisciplinary team members to ensure seamless patient care.
  • Oversee patient admission, transfer, discharge, and emergency response processes within the unit.
  • Monitor clinical documentation to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with legal and professional standards.
  • Lead quality improvement initiatives, clinical audits, incident reporting, and risk management activities to enhance patient safety and service quality.
  • Ensure the availability, proper maintenance, and safe use of medical equipment, medications, and supplies.
  • Participate in recruitment, orientation, competency assessments, performance evaluations, and ongoing education of nursing staff.

  9. Support claim quality audits, payer queries, reconciliation activities, and documentation requests, including preparation of clinical justification and supporting evidence when required.

The Phlebotomist/donor collection technician is responsible for drawing blood from patients or donors and records identity of patient or donor.

  4. Verifies or records identity of patient or donor and converses with patient or donor to allay fear of procedure.
  5. Applies tourniquet to arm, locates accessible vein, swabs puncture area with antiseptic, and inserts needle into vein to draw blood into collection tube or bag.
  6. Withdraws needle, applies treatment to puncture site, and labels and stores blood container for subsequent processing.
  7. Transports specimens in a timely manner from the collection areas of patient’s rooms to the Clinical Laboratory.
  8. Handles mild side effects or adverse reactions from patients or donors in a calm and orderly fashion to prevent harm, while promptly informing the supervisor or HOD.
  9. Follow all safety and Infection Control policies and procedures, including standard precautions, when performing phlebotomy procedures, handling biological specimens and waste disposal.
  10. Assures that the work area is maintained in an orderly manner and is cleaned and disinfected regularly to avoid contamination.

The Cardiology Technician plays a crucial role in assisting healthcare professionals in the diagnosis, treatment, and care of patients with cardiovascular conditions . This position requires a combination of technical skills, medical knowledge, and patient care expertise to ensure the efficient operation of the cardiology department.

Patient Care:

  • Perform diagnostic tests: Conduct and assist with a variety of cardiac diagnostic tests such as electrocardiograms (ECG), stress tests, Holter monitoring, and echocardiograms under the supervision of a cardiologist or other healthcare provider.
  • Prepare patients: Properly prepare patients for procedures, explaining the process, ensuring their comfort, and obtaining relevant medical history to assist in accurate diagnosis.
  • Assist healthcare providers: Collaborate with cardiologists and other healthcare professionals to provide support during procedures, answer patient questions, and ensure the smooth flow of patient care

Patient Education and Support:

  • Assesses patient educational and needs and interacts with relevant staff and departments to facilitate requirement.
  • Educate patients: Provide patients with information on cardiovascular conditions, diagnostic procedures, and lifestyle changes to improve heart health.
  • Provide emotional support and guidance to patients and families during challenging times.
  • Ensure patients understand discharge instructions and follow-up care.

Collaboration and Communication:

  • Work collaboratively with physicians, Nurses, and other healthcare team members to coordinate patient care.
  • Communicate effectively with colleagues to ensure seamless transitions of care and optimal patient outcomes.

Documentation and Record Keeping:

  • Record and document results: Accurately record test results, patient information, and other relevant data in electronic medical records (EMR) systems for review by healthcare providers.
  • Ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements regarding patient documentation.
  • Maintains patient confidentiality at all time

Safety and Infection Control:

  • Maintain equipment: Ensure that all cardiology equipment is properly maintained, calibrated, and functioning correctly to produce accurate test results
  • Adhere to strict infection control protocols to prevent the spread of healthcare-associated infections.
  • Implement safety measures to protect patients, staff, and visitors from accidents and injuries.
  • Identify and address potential safety hazards in the healthcare environment.
  • Identifies and reports defective or broken equipment, safety hazards and environmental hazards.

Professional Development:

  • Participate in ongoing training: Stay current with advances in cardiology technology, procedures, and best practices through continuous education and training opportunities.
  • Seek opportunities for professional growth and skill development through workshops, seminars, and certifications.
  • Demonstrates and maintains competence in all mandatory competencies.
  • Maintain current licensure and certifications required for the position.

Quality Improvement and Compliance:

  • Ensure compliance: Adhere to all relevant regulations, protocols, and safety standards to maintain a safe and efficient working environment.
  • Participate in quality improvement initiatives to enhance patient care and safety.
  • Demonstrates sensitivity to patient complaints and concerns. Initiates the nursing of administrative chain of command if unable to resolve patient issues
  • Assists the Head Nurse of the unit by willing acceptance of any other work-related responsibility.
  • Other duties assigned within the scope of responsibility and requirements of the job.

Skills

  • High school diploma or equivalent; certification or associate degree in cardiovascular technology or related field preferred.
  • Previous experience in a healthcare setting, preferably in cardiology or a related field.
  • Knowledge of cardiovascular anatomy, physiology, and common cardiac conditions
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. and the ability to interact effectively with patients and healthcare professionals
  • Proficiency in using electronic health records (EHR) and other healthcare technology.
  • Ability to work independently and adapt to changing patient needs and environments.
  • Attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
  • BLS certification
  • ACLS certification as needed
  • Service mindset
  • Work may involve standing for long periods, lifting/moving equipment, and interacting with patients in various states of health.
  • May require occasional evening or weekend shifts to accommodate patient schedules.

Senior Registrar – Family Medicine (Pipeline)

Family Medicine Senior Registrar will provide comprehensive primary healthcare physically and through telemedicine to individuals and families of all ages, encompassing preventive, acute, and chronic care. Will play a crucial role in diagnosing and treating a wide range of medical conditions, promoting health education and preventive measures, and coordinating care with specialists and other healthcare professionals. Additionally, will be responsible for practicing population health management and value-based care, focusing on improving patient outcomes through efficient and effective healthcare delivery through specific care programs and clinical pathways, with an emphasis on delivering patient-centered care and optimizing health outcomes.

Patient Consultations and Management

  • Conduct comprehensive telehealth consultations and in-person consultations via thorough patient history and physical examinations with patients experiencing Family Medicine and general medicine complaints
  • Provide healthcare to all family medicine target population across age and gender
  • Provide chronic diseases and preventive care consultations and follow up to patients as per clinical guidelines
  • Utilize video conferencing platforms to assess patient symptoms, review medical history, and perform virtual examinations. Develop personalized treatment plans, prescribe medications, and provide ongoing patient education

  • Utilize telehealth platforms for virtual appointments and conduct in-person assessments as needed.
  • Develop and implement personalized treatment plans, including medication management, referrals to specialists, and lifestyle modifications
  • Oversee ongoing care for chronic and acute conditions
  • Adjust treatment plans as necessary based on patient feedback and clinical outcomes.
  • Collaborate with other healthcare professionals, including primary care physicians, specialists, and nurses, to ensure seamless patient care
  • Practice population health management by identifying and addressing health issues at the community level, implementing preventive measures, and promoting health education and awareness
  • Document findings and treatment plans meticulously in patient records

Quality Assurance and Compliance

  • Communicate effectively with patients and their families, providing clear and concise explanations of diagnoses, treatment options, and follow-up care
  • Adhere to all relevant medical regulations, ethical guidelines, and quality assurance standards for telehealth practice and in-person practice
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of telehealth regulations and best practices. Participate in quality improvement initiatives and document patient encounters accurately
  • Participate in quality improvement initiatives, research activities, and clinical audits to enhance patient care and outcomes
  • Regularly review compliance protocols and participate in training sessions.
  • Collaborate with compliance officers to ensure all practices meet regulatory standards.
  • Prepare reports for audits and inspections, ensuring accuracy and completeness.
  • Stay updated on changes in healthcare regulations and implement necessary adjustments

Professional Development

  • Continuously enhance professional knowledge and skills in family medicine, in-person and telehealth best practices

Telehealth Platform Proficiency

Collaborate with IT support to troubleshoot any technical issues

Patient Safety and Satisfaction

  • Maintain satisfactory patients consultations through communication, taking complete history, providing empathy and understanding of patients conditions and circumstances, explanation of diagnosis and proposed management plan and answering patient queries
  • Monitor patient feedback and address concerns promptly.
  • Implement safety protocols to minimize risks during consultations.
  • Conduct regular training sessions on patient safety for healthcare staff.
  • Utilize patient satisfaction surveys to gather insights for continuous improvement

Collaboration with Healthcare Teams

  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to optimize patient care
  • Share insights and recommendations to support patient-centered care approaches.
  • Facilitate communication between team members regarding patient status and needs

Skills

  • Residency training in Family Medicine from an accredited program.
  • Board certification in Family Medicine.
  • Saudi Commission for Health Specialties (SCFHS) classification and registration as a Family Medicine Senior Registrar.
  • Proven experience as a Family Medicine Senior Registrar or similar role, preferably in a primary care setting.
  • Experience in practicing population health management and value-based care approaches.
  • Proficiency in using electronic medical records (EMR) and telemedicine platforms.
  • Strong clinical judgment and analytical skills.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build rapport and establish effective relationships with patients and colleagues.
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment and manage multiple priorities.
  • Commitment to ongoing professional development and staying abreast of the latest advancements in family medicine, population health management, and value-based care.

The Cast Technician plays a vital role in supporting orthopedic physicians and healthcare professionals in the treatment and management of patients with musculoskeletal injuries and conditions. The position is responsible for the application, removal, modification, and maintenance of casts, splints, braces, and other orthopedic devices to ensure optimal patient care and recovery.The Cast Technician is expected to provide patient-centered care, ensure patient safety, maintain accurate documentation, and educate patients on cast care and injury management while adhering to organizational policies and professional standards.

Patient Care:

  • Apply, remove, repair, and modify casts, splints, braces, and orthopedic immobilization devices as prescribed by physicians.
  • Assist physicians during fracture reduction procedures and orthopedic treatments.
  • Prepare patients for casting procedures and ensure proper positioning and comfort
  • Assess circulation, sensation, and movement before and after cast application.
  • Monitor patients for signs of complications related to casting or splinting.
  • Perform wound dressing changes associated with orthopedic treatment as directed.
  • Ensure patient privacy and dignity throughout all procedures.

Patient Education and Support:

  • Assesses patient educational and needs and interacts educate patients and families regarding cast care, splint maintenance, and activity restrictions.
  • Provide instructions on recognizing signs of complications such as swelling, pain, skin breakdown, or circulation issues.
  • Reinforce physician treatment plans and follow-up requirements.
  • Answer patient questions regarding orthopedic devices and recovery expectations.
  • Provide emotional support to patients experiencing injury-related anxiety or discomfort

Collaboration and Communication:

  • Collaborate with orthopedic surgeons, physicians, nurses, physiotherapists, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Communicate relevant patient observations and concerns promptly.
  • Coordinate patient flow to ensure efficient clinic operation
  • Assist in facilitating referrals and follow-up appointments as appropriate.
  • Participate in multidisciplinary discussions regarding patient care.

Documentation and Record Keeping:

  • Accurately document casting procedures, patient assessments, interventions, and follow-up instructions in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR).
  • Record materials used and any complications or concerns observed during treatment.
  • Maintain complete and timely patient records.
  • Ensure compliance with legal, ethical, and regulatory documentation standards.
  • Always maintain patient confidentiality.

Safety and Infection Control:

  • Prepare and maintain casting materials, supplies, and orthopedic equipment.
  • Ensure casting equipment is clean, functional, and properly stored.
  • Follow infection prevention and control standards during all procedures.
  • Identify and report defective equipment and environmental hazards.
  • Adhere to workplace safety policies and emergency procedures
  • Maintain adequate stock levels of casting materials and supplies

Professional Development:

  • Maintain competency in casting techniques, orthopedic procedures, and patient care practices
  • Participate in training programs, workshops, and continuing professional development activities.
  • Support quality improvement initiatives and departmental audits.
  • Contribute to patient safety and service excellence programs.
  • Assist the Head Nurse and orthopedic team with additional duties within the scope of practice.
  • Maintain current certifications required for the role

Quality Improvement and Compliance:

  • Ensure compliance: Adhere to all relevant regulations, protocols, and safety standards to maintain a safe and efficient working environment.
  • Participate in quality improvement initiatives to enhance patient care and safety.
  • Demonstrates sensitivity to patient complaints and concerns. Initiates the nursing of administrative chain of command if unable to resolve patient issues
  • Assists the Head Nurse of the unit by willing acceptance of any other work-related responsibility.
  • Other duties as assigned within the scope of responsibility and requirements of the job.

Skills

  • Diploma in Cast Technology, Orthopedic Technology, Healthcare Sciences, or related field.
  • Certification as a Cast Technician or Orthopedic Technician preferred.
  • Minimum 2 years of experience in orthopedic, trauma, emergency, or outpatient orthopedic settings preferred.
  • Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification.
  • Knowledge of musculoskeletal anatomy, fractures, and orthopedic conditions.
  • Proficiency in applying and removing various types of casts, splints, braces, and orthopedic devices.
  • Knowledge of fracture management principles and immobilization techniques.
  • Familiarity with orthopedic clinic workflows and patient care processes.
  • Knowledge of infection prevention and control practices.
  • Ability to assess neurovascular status and identify casting complications.
  • Experience using Electronic Medical Records (EMR) systems.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Effective communication and patient education skills.
  • Ability to work independently and within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Service-oriented mindset with strong interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to stand for extended periods during procedures.
  • Ability to assist with patient positioning and handling orthopedic equipment.
  • May require flexibility in scheduling to accommodate clinic operational needs.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced outpatient and orthopedic clinical environment.

• Obtains detailed patient histories, including medical, developmental, social, educational, and familial aspects.
  • Performs otoscopic examinations to assess the external auditory canal and tympanic membrane, documenting any abnormalities.
  • Immittance-Based Assessment: Conducts multi-frequency tympanometry, acoustic reflex testing (including threshold, decay), and Eustachian tube function assessments to evaluate middle ear and auditory pathway integrity.
  • Behavioral Audiometric Evaluation: Selects and performs age- and condition-appropriate behavioral tests for pediatric and adult patients. These include Visual Reinforcement Audiometry (VRA), Free-Field Audiometry, Conditioned Play Audiometry (CPA), Pure-Tone Audiometry (air and bone conduction), extended high-frequency testing, and speech audiometry (SRT, WRS in quiet and noise).
  • Retro cochlear Evaluation: Administers specialized tests (e.g., Tone Decay, SISI, PI-PB) to screen for retro cochlear pathologies.
  • Central Auditory Processing: Performs basic central auditory processing screening tests (e.g., temporal processing, auditory figure-ground tasks) where applicable.
  • Otoacoustic Emissions (OAE): Performs and interprets Distortion Product and Transient Evoked OAEs.
  • Electrophysiological Testing: Conducts auditory evoked potential assessments such as ABR, ASSR, and ECochG as part of diagnostic protocols.
  • Vestibular Assessment: Participates in vestibular testing (e.g., VNG, caloric testing, VEMP, vHIT, and post urography) as appropriate.
  • Tinnitus and Sound Sensitivity Assessments: Administers tinnitus questionnaires and audiological tests including pitch/loudness matching, minimum masking level, and loudness discomfort level testing.
  • Newborn Hearing Screening and Early Intervention: Participates in newborn hearing screening and early hearing detection programs, including diagnostic follow-up as needed.

Intervention and Management

  • Hearing Devices: Evaluates candidacy for and provide fitting, verification, programming, and troubleshooting of hearing aids, bone conduction devices, cochlear implants, and assistive listening systems.
  • Rehabilitation and Counseling: Delivers patient-centered aural rehabilitation, including counseling, auditory training, and communication strategies. Educate patients on hearing conservation and the use of protective devices.
  • Management of Specific Conditions: Supports the assessment and management of auditory processing disorders, ototoxicity monitoring, and noise-induced hearing loss, using evidence-based practices.
  • Provides ongoing support and follow-up to monitor patient progress and adapt management strategies as needed. 

Patient-Centered Service Delivery

  • Provides timely and appropriate intervention to minimize the impact of hearing loss on communication, learning, and quality of life.

Administration and Operational Support

Ethical and Culturally Competent Practice

Job Summary

The General Practitioner is responsible for providing comprehensive primary healthcare services to patients of all ages. The role involves assessing, diagnosing, treating, and managing a wide range of acute and chronic medical conditions while promoting preventive healthcare and patient education.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct comprehensive medical consultations, physical examinations, and patient assessments.
  • Diagnose and manage acute and chronic illnesses.
  • Develop and implement appropriate treatment and management plans.
  • Prescribe medications and other treatments in accordance with clinical guidelines.
  • Order and interpret laboratory tests, imaging, and other diagnostic investigations.
  • Provide preventive healthcare, health screening, vaccinations, and lifestyle counseling.
  • Monitor patients with chronic conditions and provide ongoing follow-up care.
  • Refer patients to specialists or other healthcare professionals when required.
  • Maintain accurate, confidential, and up-to-date patient medical records.
  • Recognize and appropriately manage medical emergencies and arrange referral or transfer when necessary.
  • Communicate effectively with patients and their families regarding diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis.
  • Work collaboratively with nurses, specialists, pharmacists, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Follow applicable clinical protocols, infection-control procedures, and healthcare regulations.
  • Participate in quality improvement, clinical audits, and continuing professional development.
  • Maintain professional standards, ethical practice, and patient confidentiality.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • Medical degree (MBBS/MD or equivalent) from a recognized institution.
  • Valid medical license/registration to practice as a General Practitioner.
  • Completion of required internship/residency or equivalent clinical training.
  • Relevant clinical experience in primary care or general medicine.
  • Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification; additional certifications such as ACLS may be preferred.
  • Strong clinical assessment, diagnostic, and decision-making skills.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently as well as part of a multidisciplinary team.
  • Commitment to patient safety, quality care, and professional development.

Key Skills

  • Clinical diagnosis and patient management
  • Preventive and primary healthcare
  • Chronic disease management
  • Emergency assessment
  • Patient counseling and education
  • Medical documentation
  • Communication and teamwork
  • Clinical decision-making
  • Time management and organization

metas.experience: Relevant clinical experience in primary care or general medicine.
metas.qualification: Medical degree (MBBS/MD or equivalent) from a recognized institution.

The Microbiology Technologist performs a broad range of routine and advanced microbiological testing procedures to support the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of infectious diseases. Conducts bacteriological, mycological, parasitological, and virological examinations on clinical specimens, ensuring timely, accurate, and reliable test results in compliance with established quality and regulatory standards. Works under the direct supervision of the Microbiology Supervisor and the Director of Microbiology. Participates in departmental rotation schedules to maintain competency in all areas of microbiology services.

Responsibilities

Technical Operations

  • Perform routine and specialized microbiological testing procedures for the cultivation, isolation, identification, and susceptibility testing of microorganisms from a variety of clinical specimens, including body fluids, tissue, exudates, and other patient samples. 
  • Conduct bacteriological, mycological, parasitological, and virological analyses in accordance with approved laboratory procedures and quality standards. 
  • Recognize the clinical significance of laboratory findings and ensure accurate interpretation, validation, and timely reporting of results within established turnaround times. 
  • Perform antimicrobial susceptibility testing and provide laboratory data that supports appropriate clinical management of infectious diseases. 
  • Review test results for accuracy and consistency, investigate discrepancies, and implement corrective actions when required. 
  • Promptly communicate critical, abnormal, or clinically significant results to physicians and other authorized healthcare providers in accordance with hospital policies.
  • Assesses specimen acceptability by reviewing patient preparation, collection requirements, transport conditions, storage parameters, and other pre-analytical factors. Reject or escalate unsuitable specimens in accordance with laboratory policies and quality standards.
  • Maintains accurate, complete, and timely documentation within the Laboratory Information System (LIS) and associated records.
  • Manages reagents, calibrators, quality control materials, consumables, and specialized testing kits through appropriate receipt, storage, lot verification, inventory monitoring, stock rotation, and expiry management. Assists in maintaining adequate inventory levels to ensure uninterrupted laboratory operations while minimizing wastage.
  • Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and support to students and trainees. 

Quality Assurance and Compliance

  • Performs and evaluates quality control, proficiency testing, external quality assessment activities, and other quality indicators to ensure analytical reliability and accuracy.
  • Investigates quality control failures, instrument performance issues, and non-conforming events, implementing corrective actions and documenting outcomes in accordance with laboratory procedures.
  • Ensures compliance with patient identification, traceability, confidentiality, data integrity, and document control requirements.
  • Collaborates effectively with pathologists, physicians, nursing staff, phlebotomists, laboratory colleagues, referral laboratories, and other stakeholders to ensure high-quality laboratory services and optimal patient outcomes. Provides technical support and guidance to laboratory colleagues within area of expertise.
  • Participates in continuing education, professional development, competency programs, and departmental training initiatives to maintain current knowledge and technical proficiency. Promotes a culture of safety, quality, teamwork, innovation, and patient-centered care.
  • Participates in internal audits, quality improvement initiatives, competency assessments, accreditation activities, and regulatory inspections to maintain continuous compliance with CAP, DHA, JCI, and other applicable standards.
  • Supports the investigation, documentation, and resolution of incidents, non-conformities, corrective actions, preventive actions, and risk management activities.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in medical laboratory technology/microbiology or equivalent qualification
  • Current/Valid Dubai Health Authority (DHA) License – Microbiology Technologist

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE:

  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience in Medical Microbiology.
  • Knowledge of laboratory and general computer applications is preferred.
  • Ability to speak and write English fluently.

The Flow Cytometry Scientist performs and supports high-complexity flow cytometry testing for diagnostic, prognostic, and disease-monitoring applications within the approved laboratory scope of practice. The role is responsible for specimen assessment, panel preparation, staining, instrument setup, data acquisition, quality control, analysis, technical validation, and troubleshooting to ensure the delivery of accurate, reliable, and timely results.

The Flow Cytometry Scientist collaborates closely with Pathology, Hematopathology, and laboratory teams to support patient care and clinical decision-making. The position also contributes to assay validation and verification, competency assessment, quality management initiatives, and continuous improvement activities while ensuring compliance with American Hospital Dubai policies, Dubai Health Authority (DHA) regulations, College of American Pathologists (CAP) requirements, Joint Commission International (JCI) standards, and applicable laboratory quality and safety practices.

Responsibilities

  • Performs high-complexity flow cytometry testing within the approved test menu, including applicable hematolymphoid immunophenotyping, lymphocyte subset analysis, CD34 enumeration, PNH testing, immune monitoring, Measurable residual disease (MRD) and other validated assays.
  • Reviews specimen identification, clinical information, suitability, anticoagulant, transport, storage, viability, and cellularity; escalates inadequate, compromised, or discrepant specimens in accordance with laboratory policy. Advises outreach laboratories on correct specimen/test order as applicable.
  • Prepares specimens and antibody panels, performs staining and washing procedures, and applies validated controls, compensation, fluorescence settings, and acquisition parameters to achieve reliable and reproducible results.
  • Operates, standardizes, calibrates, maintains, and troubleshoots flow cytometers and related equipment, documenting daily performance checks, maintenance, reagent status, and corrective actions.
  • Analyzes flow cytometry data using validated gating strategies and software, identifies abnormal or technically significant patterns within authorized scope, and escalates cases requiring clinical interpretation to the responsible Pathologist/Hematopathologist.
  • Supports verification and validation of new assays, antibody panels, instruments, software, reagents, reference ranges, and methodology changes, including analytical performance, carryover, sensitivity, reproducibility, and documentation assigned.
  • Maintains accurate and timely documentation in the Laboratory Information System and approved analysis platforms, ensuring patient identification, specimen traceability, data integrity, confidentiality, controlled access, and retention of raw and analyzed data.
  • Maintains adequate stocks of antibodies, reagents, controls, calibrators, consumables, and test materials through receiving, lot verification, storage, expiry monitoring, inventory control, and timely escalation of supply risks.
  • Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and support to students and trainees. 

Quality Assurance and Compliance

  • Performs and evaluates quality control, calibration, calibration verification, proficiency testing, external quality assessment activities, and other quality indicators to ensure analytical reliability and accuracy.
  • Investigates quality control failures, instrument performance issues, and non-conforming events, implementing corrective actions and documenting outcomes in accordance with laboratory procedures.
  • Ensures compliance with patient identification, traceability, confidentiality, data integrity, and document control requirements.
  • Collaborates effectively with pathologists, physicians, nursing staff, phlebotomists, laboratory colleagues, referral laboratories, and other stakeholders to ensure high-quality laboratory services and optimal patient outcomes. Provides technical support and guidance to laboratory colleagues within area of expertise.
  • Participates in continuing education, professional development, competency programs, and departmental training initiatives to maintain current knowledge and technical proficiency. Promotes a culture of safety, quality, teamwork, innovation, and patient-centered care.
  • Participates in internal audits, quality improvement initiatives, competency assessments, accreditation activities, and regulatory inspections to maintain continuous compliance with CAP, DHA, JCI, and other applicable standards.
  • Supports the investigation, documentation, and resolution of incidents, non-conformities, corrective actions, preventive actions, and risk management activities.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Medical Laboratory Science, Medical Laboratory Technology, Biomedical Science, Clinical Laboratory Science, Immunology, or a related recognized discipline; Master’s Degree is preferred.
  • Current professional registration in the home country where applicable and valid Dubai Health Authority (DHA) License/Eligibility appropriate to the professional title and approved scope of practice.
  • Advanced knowledge of flow cytometry principles, immunophenotyping, fluorochromes, antibody panels, compensation, gating strategies, specimen preparation, quality control, and instrument troubleshooting.
  • Knowledge of hematology/hematopathology, immunology, leukemia and lymphoma immunophenotyping, laboratory safety, and pre-analytical factors affecting flow cytometry results.
  • Knowledge of CAP accreditation requirements, DHA Clinical Laboratory Standards, JCI requirements, and ISO 15189 quality principles is preferred.
  • Strong analytical, technical, documentation, communication, and organizational skills with high attention to patient identification, traceability, data integrity, and confidentiality.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE:

  • Minimum of four (4) to five (5) years of recent Medical Laboratory experience, including at least three (3) years of hands-on experience in clinical flow cytometry or immunophenotyping.
  • Demonstrated experience with multicolor flow cytometry, specimen preparation, panel setup, instrument calibration, compensation, data acquisition, gating, analysis, and technical troubleshooting.
  • Experience in hematolymphoid immunophenotyping and specialized applications such as lymphocyte subsets, CD34 enumeration, PNH, or other validated clinical flow cytometry assays is highly preferred.
  • Experience in assay validation/verification, proficiency testing, quality control review, non-conformity investigation, corrective action, and accreditation preparation is preferred.
  • Experience within a tertiary, CAP-accredited, JCI-accredited, or similarly regulated laboratory environment is highly preferred.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES   :

–        Showing knowledge of all hospital policies and procedures including infection control, fire and safety, and quality improvement.

–        Showing knowledge of all pharmacy policies and procedures and participate in their development and implementation.

–        Pharmacist is responsible for assuring that all patients receive safe and rational drug therapy.

–        Dispensing medicines and medical supplies according to in-patient physician’s orders (using the unit dose system as the method of preparation) or according to ASH valid and authorized out-patient prescription or narcotic and controlled prescriptions depending on specialized training provided.

–        Reviews and interprets physician’s drug orders for clarity, accuracy, rationality, dosage form, allergies, interaction, incompatibility etc. Any questions regarding medication orders will be resolved immediately, or within reasonable time period with the attending physician to avoid delay in the therapy to the patient.

–        If the discrepancy is not resolved is responsible for referring the problem to the unit supervisor or head of pharmacy if necessary.

–        Pharmacist will review patient profile to check for appropriateness of the treatment according to patient age, weight, diagnosis and renal and hepatic function.

–        Pharmacist will carry-out compounding of sterile and non-sterile preparations in accordance to training provided.

–        When IV training is provided, pharmacist performs following strict aseptic technique, IV admixture taking into consideration compatibility of the additives with each other and with the main solution. Also, responsible to ascertain that the prescribed flow rate is within patient tolerance. Labels all IV bottles going to in-patients with complete patient’s identification, content (in Mg. mEq. or percentage) flow rate and expiration date and/or time as assigned.

–        Supervises assistant pharmacists and other Pharmacy Personnel in the work area to assure effective manpower and accountability.

–        Provides work direction for day-to-day activities and assures by constant observation that prescribed procedures are adhered to and standards maintained.

–        Preparing stock request from wards.

–        Performs monthly inspection of nursing units and other drug user units to ensure medicines are kept under proper storage conditions, discusses problems with head nurses and recommends solutions to pharmacy head.

–        Assures drug dispensing areas and drug user units are devoid of all expired or deteriorated drugs and remove them to prevent them from reaching the patient thereby contributing to patient safety.

–        Participates in quality assurance monitoring activities including medication administration, monitoring, and prescription review and medication usage evaluation.

–        Reviews drug usage patterns and suggests control when needed; advises his unit supervisor or chief pharmacist on drug usage fluctuations especially Antimicrobial in accordance to hospital ASP and drugs in the emergency list; may as authorized, make cash purchase of critical drugs from the local market.

–        Pharmacist is responsible to providing drug information to all members of health care team. Answer physicians or nursing inquiries regarding drugs. Common duties that the pharmacist may undertake includes:

–        Tablet identification

–        Giving advice on drug choice, particularly antibiotic

–        Providing dosage recommendations for elderly patients and those with renal impairment.

–        Providing information on the administration of intravenous drugs.

–        Providing compatibility information and compounding of special prescriptions.                                                                                   

–        Any questions regarding poisons overdosed must be referred to the poison center

–        Pharmacist is a source of advice and information to all medical and nursing staff regarding new medicines.

–        Pharmacist must maintain good pharmacy stock level and must follow non-available medicines, shortages and out of stock medications. Pharmacist will inform the physician of the out-of-stock situation and will suggest suitable available alternatives.

–        Pharmacist is responsible to providing medication counseling to patients especially those at discharge on the proper and safe use of medications. This can be verbal or written information to include proper use of insulin device, inhalation device medication, indication, common side effects, interactions and proper storage.

–        Pharmacist must participate in medicines safety initiatives.

Pharmacist will teach doctors on topics such as accurate prescribing, antibiotic guidelines and guidelines specific to the emergency department. Nursing staff may receive training on various subjects such as intravenous drug administration.

Graduation from accredited college of Pharmacy

Bachelor of Science Degree in Pharmacy

License to practice pharmacy in Saudi Arabia.

Job Summary:

The Clinical Staff Pharmacist – Inpatient Services provides pharmaceutical services to the hospital’s inpatients through optimizing the use of pharmaceuticals, and collaborating with healthcare professionals throughout the organization to provide the highest quality of patient care. The incumbent proactively intervenes to optimize each patient’s therapy and documents the outcome of the intervention, provides accurate drug information, ensures that pharmaceutical products and services are provided in a timely, safe and cost-effective manner and ensures compliance with current medication management standards. The Clinical Staff Pharmacist is centralized in the Inpatient Pharmacy or in one of the Satellite Pharmacies throughout the hospital.

KEY ROLE ACCOUNTABILITIES:

  • Reviews patients’ medication orders for efficacy and safety, and makes recommendations to Prescriber if changes are required.
  • Provides medication information to healthcare professionals, including but not limited to Prescribers and Nurses.
  • Verifies medication orders for accuracy and clinical appropriateness, checks medications prepared by Pharmacy Technicians for accuracy prior to dispensing and notifies appropriate persons if changes are required.
  • Participates in committees related to medication use and provides recommendations regarding various aspects of medication use process.

CLINICL:

  • Checks and verifies that medication reconciliation is completed on admission and discharge.
  • Reviews patients’ medication orders for efficacy and safety, and makes recommendations if changes are required.
  • Provides drug information to healthcare professionals, including but not limited to prescribers and nurses.
  • Performs therapeutic drug level monitoring and makes adjustments for ensuring patient safety. 
  • Consults with peers and supervisors when assistance is needed in choosing the most appropriate drug therapy.
  • Participates in drug use evaluation and drug protocol management.
  • Assesses the status of the patient’s health problems and determines whether the prescribed medications are optimally meeting the patient’s needs and goals of care.
  • Performs Drug-Drug, Drug-Lab, Drug Food and Drug-Disease Monitoring and offers alternatives when applicable.
  • Ensures continuity of care between the acute and ambulatory patient care environments.
  • Documents all clinical activities and interventions accurately and completely, as per policy and procedure.

COMPETENCY:

  • Provides in-service education to Pharmacy and non-Pharmacy personnel.

  • Has (or will obtain) certification in Basic Life Support (BLS
  • Maintains professional competency and skills sufficient to meet current and future needs of the facility.

MEDICATION SAFETY:

  • Supports and participates in the goals of the organization’s quality improvement, risk management, and patient safety programs to include (but not limited to) National Patient Safety Goals, Core Measures, and other medication-related Joint Commission International (JCI) initiatives.

OPERATIONAL:

  • Contributes to the achievement of goals of the department through personal effort and influence over others.
  • Verifies medication orders for accuracy and clinical appropriateness, checks medications prepared by Pharmacy Technicians for accuracy prior to dispensing and notifies appropriate persons if changes are required.
  • Provides accurate shift-to-shift communication regarding unsolved situations requiring future action.
  • Provides professional, courteous customer service to all customer types (patients/family, Nursing, Medical Staff, others).                        

QUALITY IMPROVEMENT:

REGULATORY:

QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS:

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Part-Time Medical Director to provide medical and clinical oversight for a specialized stem cell processing, banking and cellular therapy laboratory in Dubai.

The successful candidate must be a DHA-licensed physician with relevant experience in stem cells, cellular therapy and/or regenerative medicine.

DHA Specialty Requirement

In line with DHA requirements for stem cell services, the Medical Director must be a DHA-licensed physician specializing in:

  • Pathology
  • Haematology
  • Transfusion Medicine
  • Or another related medical field relevant to cellular therapy

The candidate should have relevant experience in cellular therapy product processing and demonstrate appropriate practical experience in stem cell processing procedures in accordance with applicable DHA requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide medical oversight for the facility’s stem cell processing and banking activities.
  • Oversee medical aspects of cellular therapy product processing.
  • Review and approve relevant medical SOPs and clinical policies.
  • Provide medical oversight regarding product suitability and release.
  • Support activities involving cord blood, cord tissue, MSCs, bone marrow, adipose-derived cells and other cellular products, where within the facility’s approved scope.
  • Provide medical and scientific guidance regarding cellular therapy and regenerative medicine.
  • Review medical incidents, adverse events, deviations and clinical risks requiring physician input.
  • Work closely with the Laboratory Director, Quality and Regulatory teams.
  • Support compliance with DHA and other applicable UAE regulatory requirements.
  • Participate in DHA inspections, audits and licensing activities when required.
  • Oversee and support staff training and competency documentation from a medical perspective.
  • Collaborate with hospitals, treating physicians, universities and research institutions.
  • Support the development and medical review of clinical research and cellular therapy programs.
  • Provide medical input into new stem cell and regenerative medicine services.

Mandatory Requirements

  • Medical Doctor (MBBS, MD or equivalent).
  • Active DHA physician license.
  • Specialist/Consultant in Pathology, Haematology, Transfusion Medicine, or another related field relevant to cellular therapy.
  • Relevant experience in stem cells and/or cellular therapy.
  • Experience in cellular therapy product processing.
  • Appropriate recent practical experience in stem cell processing procedures in line with DHA requirements.
  • Strong understanding of clinical governance, patient safety and cellular therapy standards.
  • Ability to undertake the responsibilities of Medical Director for a stem cell processing facility.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience with Mesenchymal Stromal/Stem Cells (MSCs).
  • Cord blood and cord tissue processing.
  • Bone marrow processing.
  • Adipose-derived stem/stromal cells.
  • Cell culture and expansion.
  • Regenerative medicine and advanced cellular therapies.
  • Previous experience within a stem cell bank, cellular therapy facility or cell-processing laboratory.
  • Experience with DHA regulatory requirements.
  • Familiarity with AABB, FACT/JACIE, GMP/GxP or equivalent cellular therapy standards.
  • Experience supporting clinical trials or research involving cellular therapies.

Ensures both personnel and vehicle readiness and availability to respond to accident or sudden illness or emergencies.

Responsibilities

  1. Responds to the medical emergency calls, drives to the scene and provides basic life support to the victims before they are transported to the hospital. 
  2. Evaluates the nature and extent of illness/injury to determine the right course of actions. Conduct patient assessment, 3 Lead ECG-suggestive.
  3. Provides medical aid such as AED, CPR, provide spinal motion restriction, ventilation, control severe bleeding; prevent shock, bandaging wounds, etc., to stabilize their condition. 
  4. Administration of activated charcoal, oral glucose and oxygen. 
  5. Constantly assesses the patient enroute to the emergency facility, administers additional care as indicated or directed by medical control. 
  6. Maintains vehicles and medical and communication equipment and replenishes first-aid equipment and supplies.
    1. Restocks all supplies in the ambulance and replace used blankets, linens and other supplies. 
    2. Cleans all equipment following appropriate disinfecting protocols.
  7. Continuously reassures the patient enroute to the emergency facility. 
  8. Assists all EMT paramedics in efficient advance life support care system. 
  9. Performs direct illness/injury assessment, provides basic emergency pre-hospital patient care to the ill and injured prior to and during ambulance transfer, and transfer of information to receiving facility.
    1. Maintains operational and functional readiness of ambulance unit, medical and other equipment, to ensure continuum of emergency services. 
  10. Works closely with communications officers, field supervisors, emergency department and other hospital personnel, the police department the fire dep’t., and other individuals, to deliver basic emergency and non-emergency medical services to the general public. 
  11. Respond to calls from communications dispatcher, use appropriate radio communication skills, use most expeditious route with the goal to locate the patient needing emergency services in the shortest response time possible.
  12. Assists in lifting, carrying, transporting patient to ambulance and on to a medical facility, reassuring patients and bystanders, avoiding mishandling patient and undue haste, and to provide additional emergency care following established protocols. 
  13. Follow established departmental policies, procedures and objectives, continuous quality improvement objectives, and safety, environmental, and/or infection control standards in the performance of duties.
    1. Inspect and clean ambulance and equipments; to review and restock all medical equipment to ensure their completeness and operational readiness at all times, in consultation and collaboration with field supervisor, and in compliance with safety and infection control regulations and standards. 
  14. Conducts scene size-up.
  15. Conduct primary and secondary patient examinations.
  16. Take and record vital signs.
  17. Utilize non-invasive diagnostic devices.
    1. Properly use of oropharyngeal & nasopharyngeal airway devices.
  18. Open and maintain airway by positioning the patient’s head.
  19. Provide CPR & rescue breathing for infant, children, and adults.
  20. Provide care for soft tissue injuries and control bleeding through direct pressure.
  21. Provide care for suspected fractures.
  22. Immobilization using spinal board, cervical collar, and splints.
  23. Calm down the victim’s family members.
  24. Ventilate with a non-invasive positive pressure delivery device.
  25. Provide care for suspected shock patients
  26. Perform blood glucose monitoring.
  27. Administer Epinephrine Auto Injector only for anaphylaxis or automatic injection device for anaphylaxis.
  28. Administer aspirin for suspected myocardial infarction.
  29. Operate bag valve mask device with reservoir.
  30. Perform cardiac defibrillation with an automatic external defibrillator.
  31. Perform upper air way suctioning.
    1. Understands the use of body substance isolation.
  32. Understands basic medical-legal principles.
  33. Functions within only the scope of care as defined by state, region and local regulatory agencies.
  34. Complies with regulations on the handling of the deceased, notifies authorities and arranges for protection of property and evidence at the scene.
  35. Determine that the vehicle is in proper mechanical condition.
  36. Maintains familiarity with specialized equipment used by service.
  37. Attends continuing education and refresher training programs.
  38. Complete a clear and accurate pre-hospital emergency care report from all patient contacts and provide copy of the report to the senior EMT.
  39. Perform Cardiac monitoring-3 Lead.
  40. Administer Medication via Intramuscular, Intranasal, Intravenous and via Nebulizer.
  41. Insert Intravenous Cannula and administer Crystalloids. 

Qualifications

  1. A Valid DOH License/ Exam passed as EMT in Abu Dhabi.
  2. Graduate of internationally recognized EMT – Basic course or equivalent with minimum 4 weeks (6 Weeks) duration and valid BLS Certification & PHTLS.
  3. At least two (2) years of   experience as Emergency Medical technician.
  4. Currently licensed in country of origin and with DOH license to practice in Abu Dhabi, UAE. 
  5. Fluent in spoken & written English, Arabic language is desirable, but not essential.
  6. Driving license is preferable but not mandatory.

Clinical

  • Prior to the test, explains the procedure to the patient:
  • to dress comfortably ( e.g. loose fitting, light weight clothing and sports shoes
  • not to eat a heavy meal 4-8 hours before the test
  • Asks the patient to sign a consent form as per policy.

  • Garment/s above the waist should be removed temporarily in order to attach 10 disposable electrodes.

  • Explains the test to the patient.
  • Asks the patient to remove clothing above the waist.

  • Attaches the electrodes for a two channel recording as shown in the operator’s manual. Fix the electrodes with adhesive plaster.
  • Attaches the cable lead wires following color coding as shown in the operator’s manual. Makes stress loops to prevent from pulling the electrodes.
  • After 24 hours, switch off the monitor and disconnect the patient cable lead wires from the electrodes. Take off and discard the electrodes.
  • Process the unit in the computer by typing all the necessary information about the patient, scanning and saving the ECG tracings recorded for 24 hours then to be ready for analyzing of the specialist / consultant cardiologist.

content.rendered:
Sports & Performance Medicine Physician

How we work

Our practitioners work as one team. Care at Joint Space is integrated, patient centric and focused on the whole patient journey. Our medical team is built around a functional, root cause orientation, treating the person as one connected system and using nutrition, movement, recovery and lifestyle as core tools of care, with optimisation and longevity in mind. This role sits directly beside our functional and metabolic medicine, with one physician working on the internal system and the other on structure and recovery, so that together they give our patients one complete proposition. Medical standards and direction are held by our Medical Director.

Joint Space already has the infrastructure for sports medicine, with a gym, physiotherapists, osteopaths, chiropractors, movement coaches and a full recovery space. We see a wide variety of patients, from active adults and runners to athletes and people focused on their long term health.

Our medical team currently works with:

  • Functional and metabolic medicine
  • Our Executive Check Up, offered as a basic and a premium health assessment
  • Blood testing and peptide therapy
  • Our recovery space, with sauna, cold bath, hyperbaric, red light and PEMF
  • Shared care with our physiotherapists, osteopaths, chiropractors and movement coaches

What we expect from you

  • A DHA licensed or DHA eligible physician specialising in sports or sports and exercise medicine, able to practise in Dubai
  • Real experience with active and athletic populations, from recreational to elite
  • Musculoskeletal assessment and non surgical injury management, including diagnostic musculoskeletal ultrasound
  • Competency in, or a demonstrable interest in, regenerative and image guided injectables (PRP, orthobiologics, joint and soft tissue) and performance oriented therapeutics, including peptides, where clinically and legally permissible
  • An understanding of load, adaptation and recovery, with recovery protocols, nutrition and lifestyle used as active parts of the medical plan
  • A clear plan of care for each patient that follows the Joint Space patient journey, drawing on our physiotherapy, movement, recovery and education services, with progress reviews built in so patients understand where they are and what comes next
  • A functional, root cause lens in your own practice, which is essential to how our medical team works
  • Contribution to our workshops, education and community events

What Joint Space offers you

  • The chance to develop the sports and performance medicine side of Joint Space alongside our functional and metabolic medicine
  • A clinic built around movement, with a gym, a movement space and a full recovery space to use as part of your patients’ care
  • A supporting team of physiotherapists, osteopaths, chiropractors and movement coaches who share patients and talk to each other
  • A patient base that approaches its health proactively
  • The autonomy to build your practice within our ecosystem
  • Opportunities to teach and keep developing through our workshops and our education platform

Requirements

Who we’re looking for

We are looking for a physician who enjoys the diversity of what Joint Space has to offer, from the range of patients to the disciplines and facilities working alongside them, and who wants to build sports medicine within an integrated environment where care is shared across a team. If that is the kind of clinic you want to be part of, we would like to hear from you.

Joint Space is a self pay clinic, and the role is full time and on site.

content.rendered:
The Patient Journey Coordinator helps a patient turn a practitioner’s recommendation into a booked next step. You will be present in the clinic every day, talking with patients before and after their sessions, you will receive referrals from practitioners who would like a patient to hear more about their treatment plan or about another Joint Space service that could support them, and you will follow up with phone calls and messages to our community of patients.

This is a patient facing role with booking targets and commission, and it is fully part of the Joint Space team. You will learn how our practitioners think and speak about health, what each discipline and service offers, and what we stand for, so that a patient hears the same language from you as from their practitioner. Clinical decisions stay with the practitioner, and your part is making sure the patient understands the plan, knows their options and finds it easy to continue.

You will work to the same standards as the rest of our team, which means suggesting only the parts of Joint Space that would help the person in front of you, at a time that suits them, and leaving them free to decide at their own pace.
What you will do

Engage with patients and receive practitioner referrals. You will start conversations with patients in the clinic and take referrals from practitioners, helping patients understand the treatment plan their practitioner has set and showing them which other Joint Space services can support it.

Explain services, pricing and booking options. You will know every service we offer, what it costs and how it can be booked, and you will explain this clearly so that a patient can make a well informed choice.

Understand what is holding a patient back. When a patient hesitates to book, you will find out why, help with their practical questions and concerns, and share what you learn with practitioners so that they can address it in their own conversations with patients.

Coordinate with Reception and follow up. You will work closely with Reception so that every booking is completed, and you will follow up with patients who need more time to decide.

Track your work and reach your targets. You will record every referral, conversation and booking, review your numbers regularly and work towards agreed booking targets.
Your own patient journey

You will go through the Joint Space patient journey yourself, starting in your first weeks with us. You will have your own assessment, follow your own plan and use the services you will later be explaining, so that you speak to patients from your own experience of how each one feels and what it does for you. We ask you to keep looking after your health in this way for as long as you are in the role, because patients relate most easily to someone who is on the same journey as they are.


Requirements

Who we are looking for

You enjoy talking with people and you listen well, which lets you understand what a patient needs before you suggest anything. You are comfortable discussing prices and asking for a booking, and you hold yourself to targets while keeping the patient’s interest first.

You have experience in a patient facing or client facing role where you were responsible for bookings, memberships or sales, ideally in healthcare, wellbeing or hospitality. You are organised with records and follow ups, confident with booking and messaging software, and fluent in spoken and written English.

You care about your own health, you are curious about how different clinical disciplines work together for one patient, and you want to learn. We look for Competence, Care, Collaboration, Conviction and Coherence in everyone who joins Joint Space, with honesty underneath all five.
What we offer

This is a full time role of 48 hours a week, including one weekend day each week, based at Joint Space in Alserkal Avenue. The salary is 8,000 AED a month, with commission of up to 4,000 AED a month.

The team is small, so everyone notices what each person contributes, and the standards are high. Many of our patients stay with us for years, which means you will know the people you speak to for a long time. In return, you will be part of a team that keeps to its standards and protects your time and your development.
What happens after you apply

If your application suits the role, we will send you An Introduction to Joint Space, which takes about ten minutes to read, together with our Values and Fit Questionnaire, which takes about twenty minutes to complete. An interview follows, then a practical stage in the clinic where you meet the people you would work beside, and we tell you our decision whatever it is.

Provides care for patients in Hospitals, and collaborates with physicians and other healthcare professional experts in the therapeutic use of medications. Routinely provides medication therapy evaluations and recommendations to patients and other health care professionals. Clinical pharmacists are a primary source of scientifically valid information and advice regarding the safe, appropriate, and cost-effective use of medications. Advising physicians on matters of drug usage and control within assigned hospital locations; participating in the development and delivery of continuing education programs for Pharmacy, Patient Care Services, Medical Staff and students and monitoring antibiotic usage. Participates in drug selection and maximizing therapeutic outcomes for patients. Choose alternatives in coordination with physicians.

Responsibilities

Quality and Accuracy:

  • Complies with all regulatory, safety and quality control programs and procedures applicable to the service area; including but not limited to regulatory licensing, accreditation standards, organizational policies, and procedures.
  • Advises physicians concerning the safety, appropriateness, cost-effectiveness and use of medications, and assists in the selection of the most cost-effective, evidence-based regimen case-related.
  • Acts as drug information and education resource for patients, students, colleagues, medical and nursing staff, and other healthcare professionals
  • Reports all incidents and complaints at the service level immediately for appropriate action to be taken, as per hospital policy.
  • Participates effectively in quality improvement and medication safety and medication utilization initiatives related to clinical service area.
  • Participates as required in investigational drug research programs and clinical initiatives.

Quantity/Organizational Skills:

  • Identifies and analyzes reported Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) and assists in the prevention, management, and development of process improvement.
  • Participates in patient care rounds with other members of the healthcare team daily or as assigned.
  • Prepares Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) Reports to monitor the trend and sends the report to the pharmacy director and Concerns to the committee and department.
  • Assists physicians in creating and managing the drug regimens of patients with chronic diseases. This may include, but not be limited to, activities such as meeting with patients, adjusting medication dosages, monitoring, and performing other services within the professional area of expertise. Ensure rational use of drugs and reduction of costs.
  • Locates or modifies the patient’s medication treatment plan based on scientific analysis of the patient’s condition and reports on the diagnosis of his condition.
  • Prepares an interdisciplinary care plan for patients which includes dosage adjustment, drug interactions, side effects etc.
  • Evaluates and provide recommendations on the medication treatment plan for the patient and optimal use of the prescribed therapy for both healthcare professionals in the health team responsible for the patient and the patient himself.
  • Describes any amendments to the patient’s medication treatment plan; including replacing one medical product with another, unless a written or electronic instruction has been issued by the treating physician to prevent any modification. 
  • Notifies the attending physician of the application of the treatment plan or its amendment in writing by registering the data in the patient’s record prepared within (24) hours after starting the application of the plan
  • Commits to guide patients and provide them with specialized information about their medical condition, the use of medical products, and the medication treatment plan. 
  • Provides consultation and advice to health professionals concerning their patients’ medication management plans. 
  • Identifies prescriptions that might present risks to patients and aid in resolving the relevant issues before dispensing.
  • Recognizes and discerns prescribing or administration errors, assesses potential risk and strategies to manage this risk reviews and monitors medication errors, and provides clinical validation, reporting to the pharmacy director.
  • Reviews relevant laboratory and test related to the selection and determination of the medication treatment plan and consult the primary physician to ensure that the patient is on the proper medication treatment plan, with documentation in the patient’s medical records.
  • Educates patients on the importance of medication adherence.
  • Monitors the patient’s pharmacotherapeutic regimen for effectiveness and Adverse Drug reactions and intervenes as needed.
  • Verifies and monitors medication orders for drug interactions, duplication and omission therapy, allergies, and adverse reactions, and recommends appropriate formulary alternatives as needed. 
  • Evaluates orders for parenteral nutrition and recommend modifications as indicated, in cooperation with the specialist and the clinical dietician.
  • Documents therapeutic recommendations in the patient’s medical record and pharmacy intervention forms on time.
  • Participates in standardizing clinical practice within the hospital.
  • Evaluates the medications of all assigned patients daily to prospectively evaluate all drug therapy for appropriate indications, dosage, drug interactions and drug allergies.
  • Covers weekend on-call if required.

Qualifications

  • Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm-D) or Master’s Degree in Pharmacy from an accredited University required 
  • Current license or registration to practice clinical pharmacy
  • Successful completion of a recognized Residency program or post-graduate qualifications in Clinical Pharmacy  

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE:

  • Minimum three (3) years of experience post-certification as a Clinical Pharmacist in hospital settings  
  • Knowledge of actions, side effects, appropriate use of commonly employed drugs, antibiotic utilization, evaluation, drug therapeutic monitoring, adverse drug reaction monitoring, patient chart review and selection of alternatives
  • Knowledge of current technology and pharmacy systems for distribution of medications 
  • Extensive knowledge of pharmacokinetics, pharmacotherapeutics
